svg.text: The modules in engineering_search/, by layer · every import points down the page · the web server and each MCP server have their own SearchService and share the files in .runtime/
a call at run time (the caller is above)
search.html + search.js: sign-in, search bar, folder panel
admin.html + dashboard.js: index, scan, uploads, access rules
audit.html + audit.js: audit log, page by page
style.css · app.py serves them · HTTP with a session cookie
Starts the MCP server as a
Checks the flags, then uvicorn.run(app) on 127.0.0.1
mcp_server.py · one MCP server process per client
FastMCP over stdio · 7 tools (+ coverage) · admit() per call

runtime.py · opens the stores and builds each process
stores(): index, index-<id>.lock (FileLock), queue, audit, Admission(SEARCH_BUDGET_SECONDS = 8 s)

HTTP FRONT END · WEB SERVER ONLY

Default stores if none given · uploads use queue
imports: service, access, adapters, jobs, store, core
backend_boundary checks the role on each call
SERVICE · ALL SEARCH LOGIC · NO HTTP, NO MCP, NO SQL
service.py · SearchService · one in each process
search(user, question, limit, page, mode, within)
read() · readable_files() · scan() · reindex() · status() · coverage()
admit(): a ticket, or 503 busy · save_upload() · index_upload()
Holds: index, index_lock, audit, permissions, queue, admission
lock: index reads and writes in this process
index_lock: FileLock, plan and publish, all processes
operation_lock: one scan or build at a time
imports: indexing, query, answer, sql, access, adapters, jobs, core
SEARCH LOGIC · NO FILES ON DISK
understand(question, mode) → Intent: value or list
answer(): exact sentence or table row, with status
manifest(): the answer sources for the audit
Projection: SQLite in memory, per request
INDEXING LINE · READS FILES · NEVER WRITES THE INDEX
detect.py: ContentDetector, the extension is a hint;
PDF, XLSX, DOCX and JT signatures decide type and version
status.py: statuses and hints · inventory.py: SourceFile
registry.py: default_registry(), the one list of readers
facts.py: table cells → Fact with subject, role, SI value
coverage.py: by type, version, status, folder, capability
The service publishes the plan under the index lock
complete, fail, retry · full at 1,000 jobs
WorkerPool: threads claim a job and call
BASE · IMPORTS NOTHING FROM THE PACKAGE
SearchIndex: the seam where the store is injected
to_si(): pressure in Pa, length in m
<id> comes from the document folder path · every process opens the same files
Admitted only if it fits the budget, else 503 busy
answer.understand(): one value or a list?
store.document_matches(): files with a query word
FTS5 inside the file filter, ≤ 1,000 passages
Web: JSON reply · MCP: the tool result
The path of one SQL query (tables)
app.py POST /sql, or mcp_server query_sql, admitted
The client wrote the SQL, not the service
in memory, with the permitted rows only
Audit: SQL hash, scope, cited files, no rows
get_document_evidence: the row and its passage
Reindex: POST /index, web start or MCP start
Indexer.plan(): scan, detect, choose a reader,
extract new, changed or re-read files
Failures in failed_files, with a status
store.apply(): one transaction, with the inventory
Every import points down the page.
No module imports one above it.
SQL is only in store.py, sql.py, adapters.py
Permissions and the audit are in service.py,
so both front ends give the same result.
service.py gets its stores and the index lock as
objects, from runtime.py or from a test.
indexing/ reads files only. It never writes the
index. Search code never imports it.
Each process has its own SearchService, telemetry
and Admission. They share SQLite files and a lock.
